fields.quoted_span: Generally, a housing provider may check the criminal history of an applicant, but there are some limitations. Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
fields.note: The denial standard and the factors (nature and severity, time elapsed) are also stated in the document. The mention of tenant screening companies as covered entities appears elsewhere in the document.

fields.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
fields.note: The no-blanket-ban and excluded-records parts are supported. The Jan. 1, 2020 effective date is not in D016. It comes only from the secondary DX07 document.
D016 gives no effective date for the criminal-history rules. The 2020-01-01 date is supported only by DX07, which is outside the document under review.

fields.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction
fields.note: The document describes the rules in the present tense, which implies they are in force. It does not state a status explicitly.

fields.quoted_span: The Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) covers the sale, rental, or occupancy of most housing accommodations in California, including single-family homes, multi-family homes, condominiums, apartments
fields.note: The covered parties (landlords, tenant screening companies, property management companies) and the owner-occupied one-roomer exemption are also stated in the document: "When an owner is occupying a home and is renting to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics."
The document never cites Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2, § 12264 or any regulation section. It refers only to FEHA and CRD factsheets. The rule's own review_note also says the section number is unverified.
